A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same principle-guided alignment framework, renamed from PSLE to PLE. All pages, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. v1 has no appendix; v2 includes readable proofs in Appendix A.1–A.2.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama3 8B experiments on HH, including PPL/RM results in Table 1 and training reward curves in Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains the benchmark results and adds Claude and human preference evaluations, revised training curves, and model-response case studies.

M1.justification: Equation 5 changes positive softmax reward weights into signed weights in [-1,1], allowing negative rather than exclusively positive contributions in the lower-margin training branch. Algorithm 1 also moves threshold updating outside the inner loop and replaces tau0 * alpha^t with tau0 * alpha. These change the specified procedure beyond renaming, although the implemented behavior is not established.

E1.justification: HH remains the sole benchmark, and helpful/harmless dialogue alignment remains the task. The added preference judgments and harmful/benign case-study queries assess existing task coverage without establishing a new dataset, population, language, or input environment.

E2.justification: v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2 contain the same comparators: BASE, SFT, PPO, DPO, and RAFT. The new preference evaluations use this same set; RRHF remains discussed rather than evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 50-query pairwise evaluation using Claude Sonnet and five human annotators, win/tie/loss outcomes, and order-swapped API judgments to control positional bias. It also specifies 2048 RM evaluation queries while retaining the earlier 1024-query statement, leaving the benchmark sample size inconsistent and any rerun unestablished.

E4.justification: Section 6.4 and Figure 4 add three cases examining harmful-request refusal and retained helpfulness on a benign productivity question. The existing training-curve diagnostic is also revised and discussed separately in Section 6.3. No systematic component ablations or robustness sweeps are added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added annotators and order-swapped judgments change the evaluation design rather than introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All main-table values remain identical, including OURS at PPL 8.45 and RM -0.75. v2 adds Claude win rates of 53–70% and human win rates of 54–71% across the five comparators, plus three qualitative outputs. The original-response reward trace also changes between v1 Figure 2 and v2 Figure 3, showing a smaller final guidance gap; this is not merely a relocated plot.

T1.justification: v1 claims convergence but supplies no corresponding theoretical analysis. v2 adds approximation-error and reward-margin-density assumptions, the pure-level-set definition, Lemma 5.2, Theorem 5.3, and detailed derivations in Appendix A.1–A.2. This is a substantial new theoretical component.

C1.justification: The introduction reframes the novelty claim from first identifying low generated-data utilization to first identifying overlooked coupling between generation and training. Its theoretical contribution shifts from convergence to the optimal model to a controlled-error guarantee. The abstract and introduction also remove the unsupported multiple-dataset claim, while retaining the central all-generated-data alignment claim.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the shrinking reward gap as support for threshold reduction and increasing ability to respond well without principle guidance. Its case-study discussion additionally argues that harmful-request refusal does not prevent ordinary helpfulness. No substantive failure-condition or limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents threshold 0.2, decay factor 0.9, baseline-default settings, 161K/8.55K dataset sizes, the 256-token query filter, and the 1024-token generation limit. It also specifies eight Ascend 910B devices with 64GB each and 1000GB RAM. These substantially expand reproducibility information; they do not establish changes to previously undocumented settings. Existing library links and LoRA settings remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Xu et al. (2021, 2023a, 2023b) and Zhang et al. (2021), connecting the method to label enhancement and progressive purification, and removes Liu et al. (2024) on congestion prediction. The alignment-related-work survey largely remains, with the introduction now emphasizing uncoupled generation and training as the prior-work deficiency.

P1.justification: Language revisions concentrate on the abstract, motivation, and contribution paragraphs, alongside PSLE-to-PLE renaming and smaller wording corrections. Most existing related-work, method, and conclusion prose remains. Theory and dedicated learning-curve/case-study sections are inserted without broadly reorganizing the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds a dataset-example table, two-panel preference charts, and a boxed case-study figure. It redraws the reward plot with explicit axes and a relocated legend, expands the main table with method citations, relocates Figure 1, and changes the document-wide title, heading, and header styling. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added preference evaluations and implementation disclosures improve on v1's limited empirical assessment and documentation. However, v2 introduces conflicting RM sample counts and removes progressive decay from Algorithm 1 as written. Its new proof also equates bounded reward scores with optimal-policy probabilities without justifying that identification in Appendix A.1. These issues undermine the added theoretical support and leave the unchanged benchmark scores' relationship to the revised method unclear. The PDFs therefore do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
